newsitem.title: USA: Prince George's County school plan raises concern.
newsitem.headline: Prince George's County school plan raises concern.

text.p: Developers in Prince George's County, Md., are concerned about a county school funding proposal hiking housing prices and dampening building in parts of the county, the Washington Post reported Wednesday.

Two bills before the nine-member County Council would raise money to build schools and, in some cases, prohibit the development of communities that would crowd existing or planned schools, the Post reported. A five-member council committee approved both measures last week.
Seven of the council members have indicated they will vote for the bills.
Many elected officials readily acknowledge that the development measures introduced Tuesday could bring an immediate halt to plans to build thousands of houses, the Post reported.
More than 40,000 houses have been approved for construction.
Developers say the county is threatening job growth and economic stability. The county is prohibited from increasing or creating taxes.

The one measure calls for charging $9,000 to $12,000 for each additional student a community would add to a school over 100 percent of its capacity. And the other measure would increase the fee charged to developers for new single-family homes, townhouses and apartments.
The surcharge measure would raise about $8 million a year, which could be used to float about $80 million in bonds, the Post reported.
The council's proposed six-year building program calls for spending $548 million on 50 projects to build or renovate schools. --U.S. Municipal Desk, 212-859-1650
